reason: Sender.prepare repeatedly scans contiguous revision history and hashes the same cache key twice for cache hits; avoid those costs without changing protocol or fixed policy.
changes: Use bounded contiguous sender revision arithmetic for retained-baseline membership and direct VecDeque indexing for a cache miss, instead of one or two linear scans. Receiver history may have gaps and is deliberately not changed.
Read encoded-cache hit with one HashMap.get rather than contains_key plus indexing.
Skip sender history membership work in full-only policies; preserve non-full expired-baseline statistics.
invariants: Published sender revisions are strictly consecutive from zero and oldest-only eviction preserves a contiguous window.
Only exact live attempt ACKs establish baselines. Invalid or expired baselines fall back to full.
No changes to codec, cache limits, framing, ACK queues, receiver state or application snapshot inputs.
proof: Existing contracts/codec/framing tests and full feature Clippy on existing supported toolchain.
Source-bound 8-recipient replays for every 261 fixed policy/codec configuration at sparse/loss/ACK24 and random/sync/ACK0, sizes64/2048, matching v6 all-configs cohort.
Matched 20k paired fresh-process v6/v7 observations for fixed candidates; all losses retained, no final significance/capacity acceptance while other workers are active.
claim: Exploratory optimization; not a winning universal default or proof of beating every upstream engine.
